a2953.speech: Stated that under the new administration the Ministry has been responsibly servicing the debt obligations it inherited, reporting that as of end November 2024 domestic debt payment amounted to US$36,599,733.00, external debt payment to US$47,125,555.00, and subscription payments to regional and international bodies to US$4,312,950.00.

a2953.speaker: Liberia Revenue Authority (LRA)
a2953.speech: Reporting US$619.9 million by the end of November 2024, achieving 84% of its annual target, with taxes on income and profits (US$137.2 million) and taxes on international trade (US$108.8 million) the major contributors.

a2953.speaker: Ministry of Finance and Development Planning (MFDP), Liberia (statement: “MFDP Achievements for 2024”)
a2953.speech: Stated that the MFDP, in collaboration with the Ministry of Internal Affairs, led initiatives for fiscal decentralization, including implementation of regulations under the Revenue Sharing Law mandating that 40 percent of revenues generated in each county be allocated to County Service Centers, established an administrative decentralization structure for the Local Government Law, and set up the Local Government Fiscal Board to set annual expenditure ceilings for county administrations, with ten ministries and agencies agreeing to disaggregate their budgets.

a2953.speaker: Ministry of Finance and Development Planning (MFDP), Liberia (statement: “MFDP Achievements for 2024”)
a2953.speech: Stated that the MFDP, in partnership with the Ministry of Internal Affairs and supported by various partners, conducted consultations across all 73 districts, formed the National Steering Committee on the National Development Plan and held dialogues with UN experts to align the NDP with the SDGs for 2030, with preparations underway for the formal launch of the NDP in January 2025 and the Public Sector Investment Plan and County Development Agendas drafted with support of two Liberian think tanks.

a2953.speaker: Ministry of Finance and Development Planning (MFDP), Liberia (statement: “MFDP Achievements for 2024”)
a2953.speech: Stated that the MFDP played a crucial role in the successful negotiations that enabled the government of Liberia to secure the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) Compact, a significant milestone that opens up new opportunities for development and progress.

a3097.speaker: John S. Siafa, Mayor of Monrovia
a3097.speech: Issued a clarion call for sweeping reforms to rescue Liberia's capital from decades of administrative fragmentation and fiscal dependency; invoked Monrovia's historic legacy, tracing its roots to 1822 when it was founded as Christopolis and later renamed in honor of late U.S. President James Monroe; lamented that Monrovia remains hamstrung by outdated laws, overlapping authorities, and weak institutional coordination; highlighted legal and administrative confusion stemming from multiple acts and agencies governing Monrovia and its surrounding districts; pointed to the erosion of the Monrovia City Corporation's (MCC) original mandates, such as zoning and land use, which have been absorbed by newer national agencies like the Ministry of Public Works and the Liberia Land Authority, without corresponding legal reforms; outlined five critical issues undermining Monrovia's development: unclear jurisdictional boundaries, fragmented governance, erosion of MCC's mandates, fiscal dependency on central government subsidies, and regulatory gaps; warned that these challenges have led to unplanned urban sprawl, deteriorating infrastructure, and the expansion of informal settlements, emphasising that fiscal fragmentation is particularly damaging.

a3097.speaker: John S. Siafa, Mayor of Monrovia
a3097.speech: Proposed a bold reform agenda that includes establishing a Permanent Metropolitan Coordination Body to unify city and national agencies; reforming the MCC Act to clarify mandates and eliminate overlaps; implementing fiscal reforms to increase local revenue generation and reduce dependency; integrating service delivery frameworks with clear roles and oversight; and strengthening regulatory enforcement to attract investment and improve urban standards ; concluded with a passionate appeal for action: "The urgency cannot be overstated. Monrovia's future will be determined by the choices we make now—whether we allow fragmentation and dependency to persist, or whether we commit to decisive reforms that secure strong governance, fiscal independence, and integrated service delivery."

a3287.speaker: Owen Nxumalo, Minister of Education and Training of Eswatini
a3287.speech: Has hailed Macmillan Education Eswatini as a key partner in the country’s journey toward delivering quality and culturally relevant education, describing the company’s contributions as a cornerstone of Eswatini’s educational transformation: “It is a great honour to be here today on this official visit to Macmillan Education Eswatini, a valued partner in our national journey to deliver quality education to all Emaswati.” ; “This visit is not only an opportunity to engage with our longest-standing partners but also to reflect on the impact of our shared efforts and look towards the future with renewed courage.”

a3287.speaker: Owen Nxumalo, Minister of Education and Training of Eswatini
a3287.speech: Noted that Macmillan’s location in Matsapha, Eswatini’s industrial hub, symbolized the interconnection between education and economic development, and commended the company for contributing to the local economy: “I was pleased to learn that, over and above providing quality educational materials, the company supports local entrepreneurs by procuring from them and ensuring they are paid before their due invoice dates.” ; “By publishing high-quality educational resources, Macmillan has helped develop a skilled workforce and seasoned entrepreneurs. This contribution has supported the rise of enterprises that depend on a literate and capable population, showing how education and industry can work hand in hand to drive national progress.”

a3287.speaker: Owen Nxumalo, Minister of Education and Training of Eswatini
a3287.speech: Celebrated what he termed one of the most “transformative partnerships in the history of education” — the collaboration between the Government of Eswatini and Macmillan Publishers — tracing its roots to the mid-1970s: “Before 1978, all primary school textbooks used in Eswatini were imported from South Africa, reflecting the apartheid-era Bantu Education system, a system foreign to our values, our culture, and our aspirations as an independent nation.” ; “By 1977, the NCC had successfully developed the first textbooks for Grades 1 and 2 in English, Mathematics, SiSwati, and Science. This was a defining moment, the birth of an education system built by emaSwati, for emaSwati.” ; “Importantly, all textbooks used in our primary schools today are written and developed by Eswatini’s own curriculum designers.” He also lauded the role of His late Majesty King Sobhuza II in facilitating the partnership.

a3287.speaker: Owen Nxumalo, Minister of Education and Training of Eswatini
a3287.speech: Praised Macmillan for embracing innovation by supporting the Ministry’s blended learning project and said the Ministry remains committed to building on this legacy as the country transitions toward Competency-Based Education and digital learning models. He encouraged Macmillan and other publishers to continue playing an active role in shaping the next phase of educational reform: “The future of this nation is great, especially as we work together to deliver the most prized asset that any nation can possess, a well-educated and empowered generation.” ; “As we navigate the realities of a rapidly changing world, His Majesty’s Government will continue to seek out innovative ideas from publishers such as Macmillan. Your creativity and strategic foresight are essential in preparing our learners for the future.” ; “Let me express our deepest appreciation to Macmillan Education Eswatini for its dedication to the development of our nation. May this partnership continue to flourish.”

a3375.speaker: General Staff of the Malian Armed Forces (état-major général des armées)
a3375.speech: Communicated a provisional toll of five soldiers wounded, treated by the medical services, and twenty-one terrorists neutralised ; said a significant quantity of military equipment, communications equipment, vehicles and logistics was recovered in the locality and that the air strikes also destroyed several enemy entrenchments.

a3375.speaker: General Staff of the Malian Armed Forces (état-major général des armées)
a3375.speech: Gave assurances that all measures will be taken to secure the zone durably, protect civilians, facilitate free movement and prevent any attempt by the armed groups to re-establish themselves in the region.

a3375.speaker: General Staff of the Malian Armed Forces (communiqué)
a3375.speech: In its communiqué, paid tribute to the professionalism and courage of the soldiers engaged, while stressing that the struggle for the stabilisation of central and northern Mali requires constant and determined action.

a3375.speaker: Testimonies gathered from reliable local sources and cross-checked by several Malian media
a3375.speech: According to these testimonies, living conditions in Sébabougou had become extremely precarious: supply cut-offs, restrictions on movement, violence and constant threats.

a3537.speaker: Amb. Monday Semaya, South Sudanese Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
a3537.speech: Has called for enhanced bilateral ties and cooperation between South Sudan and Germany in areas of capacity building, agriculture, education and technology, among others, and called on the German government to boost its investment in South Sudan particularly in trade through the establishment of a joint cooperation commission: “We look forward for more cooperation, particularly in the areas of capacity building, agriculture, education, technology, cultural exchanges and trade investment, including support for the peace process in South Sudan” ; “I and my government believe that we can achieve more positive and encouraging results through establishment of a joint bilateral commission, and other reliable and practical bilateral engagement.”

a3537.speaker: Amb. Monday Semaya, South Sudanese Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
a3537.speech: Encouraged Berlin to support South Sudan’s transition to lasting peace through the implementation of the 2018 peace agreement and the country’s ambition for economic reforms.

a3537.speaker: Amb. Monday Semaya, South Sudanese Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
a3537.speech: In a speech during German Unity Day, commended the European nation for being one of the first countries in the world to recognize the independence of South Sudan on July 9, 2011, and appreciated the government of Germany for its humanitarian efforts, including the contribution of its police to the UN peacekeeping mission in South Sudan.

a3605.speaker: Professor Alaric Togba, Governance Commission Acting Chairman
a3605.speech: Speaking at the program marking the end of the dialogue, stressed the need for the authority to demarcate Monrovia and provide its statutory mandates. ; Professor Togba disclosed that participants have agreed that there is an urgent need to review the mandates of institutions that have similar mandates to the Monrovia City Corporation.

a3605.speaker: Participants at the two-day policy dialogue
a3605.speech: agreed on the importance of political and administrative reorganization of Monrovia City to align with other cities in international best practices. During the two days, concerns were raised about the duplication of functions, service delivery gaps, unclear jurisdictions, fragmented governance, revenue collection disputes, erosion of mandates, and overlap of administrative boundaries. Other concerns included legal inconsistencies, weak regulatory enforcement mechanisms, the use of electoral districts as administrative districts, and the recentralization of decentralization.

a3605.speaker: Professor Alaric Togba, Governance Commission Acting Chairman
a3605.speech: According to Professor Togba, the Governance Commission considers that participants at the two-day policy dialogue reached the understanding that there is a pressing need for the political and administrative reorganization of Monrovia. He encouraged leaders and stakeholder engagements on actionable steps regarding the way forward. Professor Togba also stressed the imperative for concrete agreements and decision-making processes on what needs to be done to improve Monrovia City and make it a better and safer place for future generations. ; “Clearly, there are disturbing ambiguities and conflicting ideas about the demarcation of Monrovia that require authoritative clarification. Undeniably, addressing the foundational challenges we face will require a review of the constitution of Liberia and a review of the mandates and functions of institutions and agencies that have roles and responsibilities for managing affairs and providing services in Monrovia city,” he added. ; He pointed out that the city government of Monrovia needs to be reorganized, properly coordinated, and better monetized for the promotion of development.

a3605.speaker: Governance Commission (Liberia)
a3605.speech: also pointed to the lack of knowledge and understanding as a national issue that can no longer be ignored and emphasized that public education and awareness demand the reintroduction of the teaching of government and civics in the schools.

a3800.speaker: Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, President of the United Arab Emirates (federal decree)
a3800.speech: Issued a federal decree establishing the United Arab Emirates International Aid Agency, affiliated with the International Humanitarian and Charity Council, enjoying an independent legal identity and full capacity to act, and charged with implementing foreign aid programmes in light of the general policy on international humanitarian affairs, as well as planning, supervising, implementing and monitoring official government support, development projects and initiatives, rapid recovery and resettlement programmes, and humanitarian and relief response plans.

a3800.speaker: Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Vice-President and Deputy Prime Minister of the UAE and Chairman of the Presidential Court
a3800.speech: Stressed that the founding of the United Arab Emirates International Aid Agency was a continuation of the humanitarian approach established by the founding father, the late Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan, an approach that reflects the commitment of the United Arab Emirates to meeting humanitarian challenges and promoting sustainable development at the global level ; declared: "The United Arab Emirates pursues this path under the wise leadership and continued support of His Highness Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, President of the United Arab Emirates, which confirms the commitment of the leadership, the government and the people to promoting this noble humanitarian path."

a3800.speaker: Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of the UAE
a3800.speech: Explained that the creation of the United Arab Emirates International Aid Agency is an affirmation of the central and continuing role of the United Arab Emirates in providing vital aid, in improving living conditions and in supporting communities and peoples on all continents ; underlined the willingness of the United Arab Emirates to work side by side with international partners in order to direct joint efforts towards the creation of tangible and lasting positive change and impact, particularly in regions suffering from crises and instability, focusing on basic areas of life such as educational services, health facilities and infrastructure sectors with the aim of achieving development and prosperity for peoples.

a3800.speaker: Sheikh Theyab bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Deputy Chairman of the Presidential Court for Development Affairs and Families of Martyrs and Chairman of the International Humanitarian and Charity Council
a3800.speech: Stressed that the creation of the United Arab Emirates International Aid Agency is an enhancement of the pioneering humanitarian action of the United Arab Emirates in the world ; stressed that the Agency aims to continue to enrich foreign aid of global priority and to maximize its positive effects in the implementation of humanitarian aid programmes, initiatives and development projects in various regions of the world, in keeping with the role and position of the United Arab Emirates in humanitarian and development work at the regional and international levels.

a3800.speaker: Official reports and recorded figures (UAE)
a3800.speech: Show that since their founding by the late Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan, the United Arab Emirates have provided more than 360 billion AED (98 billion USD) in foreign aid in various humanitarian fields and development sectors, benefiting more than one billion people in different parts and regions of the world.

a3816.speaker: Dr. Mohamed Abchir, WFP Resident Representative
a3816.speech: said the initiatives are significant in creating jobs, fostering entrepreneurship, and building resilience among South Sudanese youth and women; he noted the impact of previous initiatives supported by the AfDB and emphasised the importance of investing in local agriculture and job creation to reduce humanitarian needs: “The objective of this job creation program using the small and medium enterprises is also to build the resilience of the population” ; “We see more and more program now coming through that window of resilience building and development which are really quite important here in South Sudan” ; “We’ve seen some of the impact and the results of previous programs supported by the African Development Bank and we are going to build on the results but also on the lessons learned from that previous support.”

a3816.speaker: Themba Bhebhe, African Development Bank Country Manager
a3816.speech: revealed that a future $10.6 million grant would go toward improving water and sanitation services, a critical need in Juba and other areas: “Today we are signing three operations as my colleagues have said. The water and sanitation one is 10.6 million, the women and youth is about 5.4 million and about 500,000 grant which WFP would administer” ; “So this is about 16 million that we are signing today. But our plan, probably as you are aware Minister, for the first time the Bank has approved seven projects in one year.”

a3816.speaker: Themba Bhebhe, African Development Bank Country Manager
a3816.speech: announced the AfDB’s approval of a $200 million energy project, including a 300-kilometer transmission line to import electricity from Uganda, aimed at reducing South Sudan’s high electricity tariffs, which are among the highest in the region, and improving energy access.

a3816.speaker: Albino Atak, Minister of Humanitarian Affairs
a3816.speech: expressed gratitude to development partners for their response to the humanitarian crisis caused by floods and the influx of refugees from Sudan: “This year, the floods have affected about 1.4 million people and displaced almost 400,000 people. And the effects of floods are still there up to now” ; “We are even struggling now to respond to them but also to respond to recovery. Recovery process is difficult. So with the presence of developmental partners I think we will also be able to put something for recovery.”

a3885.speaker: Robert Mugabe, former Zimbabwean President
a3885.speech: Condemned Black South Africans for only pulling down the statue of Cecil Rhodes as an attack on pro-apartheid leaders, but rather choosing to engage in xenophobia attacks and killing Black African migrants from countries that fully funded their struggle against apartheid.

a3885.speaker: Julius Malema, South African politician (EFF leader)
a3885.speech: Visited Ghana on January 23, 2024 and first warned Ghanaians never to support Israel and went on to invite them to South Africa adding that there is no xenophobia there. "He cleverly left out Operation Dudula from the conversation."

a3885.speaker: Ling Shepherd, communication officer of Triangle Project (South African LGBTQ+ organisation)
a3885.speech: Said the #ShowGhanaLove campaign is an act of queer solidarity and response to rising hate and threat of criminalisation of LGBTQ+ in Ghana ; Shepherd added that the project believes that love is not a threat and hate is.

a3885.speaker: African Union (AU) and the United Nations (UN)
a3885.speech: Non-response: "The African Union (AU) and the United Nation (UN) have not made any statement to condemn South Africa over its xenophobic activities."

a3885.speaker: South African political parties and politicians
a3885.speech: Non-response: "No political party or politician as come to condemn this group [Operation Dudula] which is gaining great prominence across the country"; "no political party can boldly speak against" xenophobia.

a3912.speaker: Tatiana Dovgalenko, Head of the Africa Partnership Department of the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a3912.speech: Said in an interview with RIA Novosti that Russia, because of sanctions, was unable in 2024 to send money for food aid to African countries such as Zambia, Zimbabwe, Mozambique, Namibia, Niger and Sudan; that Russia provides humanitarian aid to African countries in need through bilateral channels and through international organisations, including the United Nations World Food Programme (WFP), which she specified is for Moscow a key multilateral channel for delivering such aid: "The Government of the Russian Federation allocated to the programme the necessary financing for the supply of domestic food products in Zambia, Zimbabwe, Mozambique, Namibia, Niger and Sudan. However, because of the sanctions imposed by Washington in November 2024 on Russian financial institutions, including those that serve our donor projects in international organisations, it has not yet been possible to transfer the funds" ; recalled that since 2020 Russia sends the WFP an annual contribution of 10 million dollars, and last year was no exception.

a3912.speaker: Tatiana Dovgalenko, Head of the Africa Partnership Department of the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a3912.speech: Added: "This situation clearly illustrates the falseness of Western declarations about so-called 'humanitarian exemptions' and the 'targeted' character of the illegal unilateral restrictions against Russia."

a3912.speaker: Tatiana Dovgalenko, Head of the Africa Partnership Department of the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a3912.speech: Stressed that Moscow was taking measures to find a solution to these problems and that, as soon as the question of transferring Russian donor funds was settled, the WFP would coordinate with the governments of the recipient countries on the range of food products needed and suppliers would meet those requests.

a3997.speaker: Christopher Hitchens, writer
a3997.speech: Famously said that what could be asserted without evidence could be dismissed without evidence.

a3997.speaker: Dina Pule, Minister of Communications (South Africa)
a3997.speech: At the Monday press conference, repeatedly denied all wrongdoing, and claimed that Sunday Times investigative reporters Mzilikazi wa Afrika and Stephan Hofstatter had tried to blackmail and bribe her, and also attempted a honeycomb trap on two separate occasions to extract information from her ; her defence is that the paper is in bed with corrupt businesspeople and politicians who are seeking to pervert the department's tender process for their benefit, and that its investigative journalists are dishonest and downright criminal in their conduct.

a3997.speaker: Dina Pule, Minister of Communications (on Mzilikazi wa Afrika's business ties)
a3997.speech: Said that Wa Afrika was clearly being ‘handled’ by businesspeople within the industry: “You will recall that a few years ago, Wa Afrika was fired by the former Sunday Times editor Mondli Makhanya for conflict of interest because of his tendency to develop unsavoury ties with sources. While he was out of work, Wa Afrika became involved in many business ventures and pursued various business opportunities. It is these extensive business networks that Wa Afrika pursued that have now come back to disgrace the Sunday Times” ; “We have established that one of the business opportunities Wa Afrika pursued involved importing cheap cellphones from China. The Department oversees the regulation of the cellphone industry. At the centre of the cellphone venture were these prominent business people who have developed an insatiable appetite in the set-top-box tender” ; “Officially, Wa Afrika is supposed to be no longer involved in business. However, he has maintained networks with prominent business people. Wa Afrika's return to the Sunday Times as a journalist has given his network of associates and friends a media ally whom they use to further their financial interests” ; said that Wa Afrika's associates were people who were currently bidding to win the set-top-box tender.

a3997.speaker: Dina Pule, Minister of Communications (on the Sandton meeting and the alleged bribe offers)
a3997.speech: Said that at the meeting arranged in a Sandton hotel the day after the story ran, the Sunday Times journalist promised to quash incriminating information about her if she gave him incriminating information about President Jacob Zuma or the state-owned companies she oversees ; “For the record, I rejected all of the proposals made by Wa Afrika and his associates during the meeting in Sandton, as I found them to be highly unethical and inappropriate. I also felt offended by the fact that Wa Afrika and his associates saw nothing wrong in making such proposals to me” ; also claimed that a “brother” of Wa Afrika repeatedly called her to say that he could prevail upon the Sunday Times journalist to abandon the investigation, and that the man made a sexual advance which she rejected ; “After this meeting, I managed to confirm that the real intention of this woman and Hofstatter was to plant her in my office as Special Adviser with the hope that they would be able to find some wrongdoing on my part” ; “We [are] also equally aware that Sunday Times journalists have friends within my department and in the various state-owned entities, some of whom have an axe to grind for whatever reason.”

a3997.speaker: Dina Pule, Minister of Communications (on resigning and on going to the police)
a3997.speech: Despite claiming that she was offered bribes and blackmailed in order to serve a certain business interest, said that she had not contacted the police, and promised to approach the press ombudsman at some point ; explained her decision to wait so long before responding to the Sunday Times by saying she had been happy to wait for the outcomes of the parliamentary and Public Protector probes before making pronouncements, but the paper was not, so she decided to “do to them what they did to me” ; when asked if she would resign, said: “I am not thinking of resigning. There is not a shred of evidence against me.”

a3997.speaker: Sunday Times (newspaper, 24 March 2013 story “Fire Pule Now, Mr President”)
a3997.speech: “A Sunday Times investigation this week uncovered evidence of an internal audit showing that Mngqibisa engineered getting friends and relatives on the boards of the Post Office, Sentech, Usasa and the SABC with the full knowledge of Pule - offering decisive evidence of just how unsuited the minister is to her job” ; “The evidence is supported by five independent sources - several of whom serve on these boards, executive committees and top communications department posts. All spoke on condition of anonymity.”

a3997.speaker: Sunday Times (response to Pule's press conference)
a3997.speech: Responded to Pule on Monday afternoon, denying that Wa Afrika initiated meetings with the minister, or offered to suppress information he had, or indeed used a relative to get to her ; “We find it unfortunate that rather than dealing with the essence of the claims against her, she proceeds to attack the messenger of the stories. We also find it disturbing that the Minister would use her office to call an ‘important’ press conference, as she did today, to launch a personal attack on both the Sunday Times and its journalists.”

a3997.speaker: Businesspeople/associates of Wa Afrika (unnamed, as reported by Pule)
a3997.speech: Before the first story was published last year, the same associates contacted Pule to offer to make the story disappear, allegedly saying: “Minister, we can help you manage that young man, Mzilikazi, because he is our man. We raised him.”

a3997.speaker: Press ombudsman (ruling, December)
a3997.speech: Dismissed Mngqibisa's case, ruling that “in light of their silence about the nature of their relationship, the newspaper cannot be blamed for thinking that the facts pointed to a personal one”.

a3997.speaker: Mzilikazi wa Afrika, Sunday Times investigative reporter
a3997.speech: Said in an interview with Radio 702 on Monday midday that there was no smear campaign against the minister, but that new information kept springing up from many sources as it unfolded: “Week in, week out we get additional information from people. We have dozens of sources… this is not a focus on one person. We keep following it up till it is over. That is how you do an investigation.”

a3997.speaker: Ralph Mathekga, political analyst
a3997.speech: “She has every reason to look elsewhere to avoid responsibility for these allegations. She feels like her job is on the line” ; “The allegations against the Sunday Times do not change anything. Irrespective of the issues she has raised [about Wa Afrika's record], there are telltale signs within the department and state-owned entities like the SABC” ; “In my opinion she is not a fit and proper person to lead this department.”

a4041.speaker: Human Sciences Research Council (HSRC) first national survey, 2002
a4041.speech: Found that just over 11% of participants' blood samples tested positive for HIV, a finding that helped decision-makers understand how big the problem truly was - and which Aids denialists could not argue with.

a4041.speaker: Salim Abdool Karim, director of the Centre for the Aids Programme of Research in South Africa (Caprisa)
a4041.speech: Says the HSRC's 2002 national survey was "a turning point": "At a time when [the] country had a high level of denial - or more appropriately, denial at high levels - this survey began to make HIV real." ; "you cannot advise [...] public health leaders or politicians about what to do, if you don't have good evidence."

a4041.speaker: Olive Shisana, former director general in the national health department and former CEO of the HSRC, currently special advisor for social policy in President Cyril Ramaphosa's office
a4041.speech: "We went to the office of the president with our findings." ; "We told them that HIV is the reality in South Africa and that we need to do something about it - and we did."

a4041.speaker: HSRC latest household survey on HIV
a4041.speech: Shows that one in nine young people were sexually active by the time they turned 15, and that just over a third of the teen girls who have sex with men said their partners were at least five years older than them.

a4041.speaker: Yogan Pillay, director for HIV and TB delivery at the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation
a4041.speech: Says that apart from "taking our foot off the pedal", Covid also added to the slowdown in ARV uptake.

a4041.speaker: Mitchell Warren, head of the international HIV advocacy organisation Avac
a4041.speech: "We're seeing treatment scale-up go quite quickly, [but] we're not seeing the level of new infections go down as quickly - and that's a cause for great concern."

a4041.speaker: UNAids
a4041.speech: Says shrinking budgets are a problem too, with the world having about $10-billion (around R180-billion) too little to spend on HIV prevention and treatment; "Cuts in resourcing and a rising anti-rights push are endangering the progress that has been made [towards ending Aids by 2030]," read the agency's statement accompanying the release of their latest report in July.

a4041.speaker: Mitchell Warren, head of the international HIV advocacy organisation Avac
a4041.speech: Warns that under the new Trump administration in the United States it's probably "safe to say" that there will be cuts in government spending in the US - including for programmes such as the President's Emergency Plan for Aids Relief (Pepfar), which funds HIV programmes in African countries, including South Africa. "The issue is what gets cut, how quickly it gets cut, and what gets cut in a way that isn't with strategy. If financial cuts mean people fall out of treatment, it would be a disaster. We can't lose people; in fact, we need to get more people into treatment programmes."

a4041.speaker: Modelling study on HIV treatment and mortality
a4041.speech: Shows that a big part of the increase in life expectancy up to 2014 is directly because of HIV treatment becoming available, and that there would have been 1.72-million more HIV-linked deaths between 2000 and 2014 if ARVs had not been available; it also highlights that about 500 000 more HIV-linked deaths could have been prevented up to 2014 "if South Africa had moved swiftly to implement WHO [World Health Organisation] guidelines and had achieved high levels of [treatment] uptake", with the authors' calculations showing that at least 40% of such deaths in 2014 were in people who had been diagnosed but had not started treatment yet.

a4041.speaker: Mitchell Warren, head of the international HIV advocacy organisation Avac
a4041.speech: Says what's become clear now is that the world, and also South Africa, can no longer just continue as before and expect new HIV infections to decline faster: "We have to think differently. One of the things we have to do is reimagine prevention programmes." ; notes of lenacapavir that experts expect it could "get approved sometime by the middle of next year" and that "It could be a game changer - if the world moves fast enough." ; urges: "We need to begin preparing today, because I would argue that we have spent a decade squandering the opportunities of a daily [prevention] pill, a monthly ring and the two-monthly injectable [CAB-LA]. If we want to bring the number of new infections down, we cannot afford to squander this opportunity too."

a4041.speaker: Khadija Jamaloodien, the national health department's head of procurement
a4041.speech: Told Bhekisisa in October that they're considering publishing a formal request for manufacturers to say at which price they can provide the product, how much of it they can make and what they will charge for it, before Sahpra's process has been concluded.

a4050.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of Benin
a4050.speech: declared that the next elections cannot be held without the Lepi. "As regards the convening of the electorate, my government awaits referral by the Cena, which is ready to do so as soon as the conditions are met, chief among them the availability of the Lepi to be produced by the Cos-Lepi, a list which is the trigger for our entire electoral process." He stated it is urgent that the Cos-Lepi make the Lepi (Permanent Computerised Electoral List) available and that parliament agree to pass a derogatory law. He gave assurances that it falls to all political and social forces and to the government to create favourable conditions for holding the communal, municipal and local elections, as well as the legislative and presidential elections.

a4050.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of Benin
a4050.speech: said the country experienced sustained growth in real terms of around 5.6% on average over the 2012-2014 period, specifying that this was the highest rate ever recorded in Benin since independence.

a4050.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of Benin
a4050.speech: spoke about employment, with the establishment of Anpe branches in all departments, and about justice and the many efforts made in the fight against corruption.

a4050.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of Benin
a4050.speech: acknowledged that new challenges await the government he leads. "This is the place to call once again and insistently on the political class, civil society actors and the whole population to recall the ideals of the national conference of the nation's vital forces. It is for all of us to place the higher interest of the Nation above everything and to work accordingly to safeguard national concord."

a4050.speaker: Board of Directors of the US Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a4050.speech: recognised Benin's anti-corruption efforts and has just declared Benin eligible for support of 250 million US dollars.

a4050.speaker: Mathurin Coffi Nago, President of the National Assembly
a4050.speech: gave the introductory remarks before President Boni Yayi delivered his message to the Beninese people on the state of the nation.

a4111.speaker: MCC Candidate Country Report for Fiscal Year 2026 (Millennium Challenge Corporation)
a4111.speech: According to the report, released in Washington in August 2025, Ghana is ineligible to receive U.S. foreign assistance under section 7012 of the Fiscal Year 2025 State, Foreign Operations and Related Programs Appropriations Act.

a4111.speaker: Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a4111.speech: explained that while Ghana met the income threshold for consideration, the legal prohibition automatically disqualified the country from compact eligibility because of debt default.

a4295.speaker: National Democratic Congress (NDC), Ghana (petition to the Electoral Commission)
a4295.speech: Petitions the Electoral Commission for an urgent forensic audit of the 2024 voters register and its IT system, presenting “alarming irregularities, discrepancies and unauthorised manipulations discovered in the 2024 Provisional Voters Register” which “pose a significant and immediate threat to the credibility of the 2024 General elections”; states the irregularities “are not minor oversights or clerical errors; they indicate a deliberate manipulation of the voter database” ; says it has uncovered 243,540 illegal transfers, over 15,000 unidentifiable voter transfer paths, 3,957 deleted registered voters, 2,094 misplaced voter transfers and corrupt data files, and that five Biometric Voter Registration laptops were stolen from the EC Headquarters under CCTV surveillance ; complains the EC failed to provide the Provisional Voters Register in time for scrutiny, opened nominations prematurely on the provisional register, and rejected the NDC’s request for a live broadcast of the party’s findings ; demands an independent forensic audit of the register and its IT system, a stakeholder meeting with all political parties, civil society organizations and key international stakeholders (including ECOWAS, AU, UNDP, EU, USAID, The British High Commission and others), publication of the audit findings, a 5-day re-exhibition of the register, reversal of all unauthorized transfers, a revised electoral timeline, and accountability and integrity measures.

a4295.speaker: Electoral Commission of Ghana (press conference, 2nd September 2024)
a4295.speech: Acknowledged some of these errors and admitted to errors and illegal voter transfers during a press conference, but justified these mistakes as correctable during the exhibition exercise.

a4295.speaker: Dr Bossman Asare, Deputy Chairman of the Electoral Commission of Ghana
a4295.speech: Publicly admitted to the existence of illegal voter transfers and inflations in the voter transfer list during the 2nd September 2024 Press Conference, but indicated that the EC is working on it.

a4358.speaker: Abiy Ahmed, Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a4358.speech: Pledged before parliament to close no less than 31 missions abroad ; "Instead of spending all the forex here and there on the embassies, at least 30 of them should be closed, and the ambassadors can work from here," said the PM during the parliamentary session on July 5, 2021 ; has made his misgivings public about the running cost of diplomatic missions.

a4358.speaker: Dina Mufti, spokesperson of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a4358.speech: Described the closures in a manner he called "rightsizing" instead of downsizing ; dismisses claims that the decision came abruptly with no formal study, saying the decision was made based on the findings of a study conducted by a committee ; argued that the reform should not be termed a downsizing, choosing instead to employ the word "rightsizing."

a4358.speaker: Dina Mufti, spokesperson of the foreign office (weekly briefing)
a4358.speech: "Members of foreign missions have been recalled and will go through re-training," said Dina Mufti during a weekly briefing held last Thursday.

a4358.speaker: A diplomat (anonymous)
a4358.speech: Claimed that the decision to downsize came abruptly, with no formal study carried out, unlike during previous reforms when the Ministry would deploy professionals to determine the path to follow.

a4358.speaker: Another diplomat (anonymous)
a4358.speech: "In the Ministry's century-old history, there has never been a 'restructuring' of this magnitude," adding that the sudden nature of the closures has been a challenge in terms of settling personal matter and official duties.

a4358.speaker: A diplomat (anonymous)
a4358.speech: "It is natural that the closure of over half of the diplomatic missions in such an abrupt and unprecedented manner will have an impact on our diplomacy."

a4358.speaker: A foreign policy expert who requested anonymity
a4358.speech: Says such a practice is common in light of a change of government as ideologies and relationships with countries evolve and it should not be thought of as a catastrophic phenomenon ; "There were times the country had very few missions, and at times it was oversized," he said. "The critical issue is finding balance." ; according to the expert, the closure of missions is not a black and white matter that should be classified as either right or wrong, and he added that while some of the closures might indeed be a wise decision, others, such as the embassy closure in Cairo, could spell trouble in securing national interests.

a4358.speaker: Sources close to the matter (anonymous)
a4358.speech: Some diplomats have chosen not to return, according to sources close to the matter.

a4358.speaker: Sources close to the matter (anonymous)
a4358.speech: The consular office in Los Angeles has already shipped cars, laptops and other movable properties to the embassy in Washington DC, according to sources close to the matter.

a4358.speaker: People familiar with the process (anonymous)
a4358.speech: Following the reorientation, there will be a redeployment of diplomats to missions, but a significant number of those recalled will be assigned to federal agencies, according to people familiar with the process.

a4586.speaker: Moustapha Mohamed Mahmoud, Djiboutian Minister of National Education and Vocational Training (MENFOP)
a4586.speech: On the sidelines of the handover of the donation, expressed his gratitude to the US ambassador for the US government's valuable support to his department and the solid working relations they have established with USAID.

a4598.speaker: Global Fire Power Index 2024 (report)
a4598.speech: According to the Index, which considers over 60 individual measurement factors including the quantity of military units, financial standing, logistical capabilities, and geography to determine countries' scores, smaller, technologically advanced nations can effectively compete with larger, less developed nations; it provides the rankings, active soldier numbers and defence budgets cited for Egypt, Algeria, Nigeria, Morocco, South Sudan, DR Congo, Ethiopia, Angola, Sudan and Tunisia.

a4675.speaker: Airport official (anonymous)
a4675.speech: Told the AFP news agency on condition of anonymity that international flights would resume on December 24, following maintenance work.

a4675.speaker: Mohammed al-Bashir, newly appointed Prime Minister of Syria
a4675.speech: Has said he will remain in office until March.

a4675.speaker: Geir Pedersen, United Nations Special Envoy for Syria
a4675.speech: Called for “free and fair elections” in Syria after the transition and urgent humanitarian assistance for the country ; warned on Tuesday that the war has not yet ended ; told reporters in Damascus that “there is a lot of hope that we can now see the beginning of a new Syria”.

a4675.speaker: Geir Pedersen, United Nations Special Envoy for Syria
a4675.speech: Expressed hope for a “political solution” in the Kurdish-held northeast, where the US-backed, Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) are battling Turkish-backed groups.

a4675.speaker: Murhaf Abu Qasra (Abu Hassan al-Hamawi), HTS military chief
a4675.speech: Speaking to AFP, said Kurdish-held areas would be integrated under the country’s new leadership, adding that the group rejects federalism and that “Syria will not be divided” ; “The Kurdish people are one of the components of the Syrian people … Syria will not be divided and there will be no federal entities.”

a4675.speaker: Murhaf Abu Qasra (Abu Hassan al-Hamawi), HTS military chief
a4675.speech: Said the group would be “the first” to dissolve its armed wing and integrate into the armed forces.

a4675.speaker: Hadi al-Bahra, head of the Syrian National Coalition
a4675.speech: Said on Wednesday that Syria’s transitional government should be credible and not exclude any Syrian party or be based on sectarianism.

a4675.speaker: Hadi al-Bahra, head of the Syrian National Coalition
a4675.speech: Told journalists at a news briefing that the Turkiye-based Syrian National Coalition would return to Syria and set up headquarters there, adding that he intended to return as well ; “Logistics should be worked out and freedom of speech should be guaranteed.”

a4675.speaker: UN Security Council (statement)
a4675.speech: In a statement, members called for the implementation of “an inclusive and Syrian-led and Syrian-owned political process” that they said should meet the legitimate aspirations of all Syrians, protect all of them and “enable them to peacefully, independently and democratically determine their own futures.”

a4675.speaker: UN Security Council (statement)
a4675.speech: The 15-member body emphasised battling “terrorism” across the country, stressing that Syria must abide by council resolutions on non-conventional weapons and reiterating support for UN peacekeepers and the inviolability of diplomatic premises.

a4808.speaker: Government of Zambia
a4808.speech: Has disclosed that collaborating partners and some financial institutions have shown interest to develop the livestock and fisheries sectors in the country.

a4808.speaker: Bradford Machila, Minister of Agriculture and Cooperatives in charge of livestock and fisheries
a4808.speech: Said support in infrastructure development, camp house rehabilitation and laboratory construction in the two sectors will improve Zambia’s economy. He named the financial institutions that have pledged to support the livestock and the fisheries sectors as the African Development [Bank] and the World Bank, and said the other collaborating partnerships, such as the European Union, COMESA, USAID and SADC have also shown willingness to support Zambia in the fisheries and livestock sectors.

a4808.speaker: Bradford Machila, Minister of Agriculture and Cooperatives in charge of livestock and fisheries
a4808.speech: Stated that the new ministry of livestock and fisheries expected to be established is committed to deliver better services to the country that will enhance economic development. He noted that government’s commitment to ensure development in the two sectors has been evidenced by increased funding allocated to the two sectors. “Government is in a hurry to develop the livestock and fisheries sectors and we should all apply ourselves diligently to meet the objectives and targets in the newly established ministry of agriculture and cooperatives in livestock and fisheries.”

a4808.speaker: Bradford Machila, Minister of Agriculture and Cooperatives in charge of livestock and fisheries
a4808.speech: Clarified that government has prioritized the disease control programme in the livestock sector before lifting the livestock movement ban. He noted that the ministry will focus on prevention of diseases than control, and that control measures of diseases will still be undertaken but emphasized that it was better to prevent the diseases. He, however, regretted the inconvenience that might have been caused to farmers by instituting a livestock ban but maintained that government was taking disease prevention and control by putting in place a movement ban of animals as a matter of urgency and high priority. The minister said that vaccination programmes against diseases will be continued by the veterinary department to curb animal diseases.

a4864.speaker: Ato Neway Beyene, Secretary General of the board of Saint George Sports Association
a4864.speech: Announced that the general assembly had officially begun; the reason the other board leaders were absent was not explained.

a4864.speaker: Ato Neway Beyene, Secretary General of the board of Saint George Sports Association
a4864.speech: Gave clarification on the questions raised, explaining that a general assembly had not been held for so many years because in the first years of the COVID-19 pandemic and the war that broke out in northern Ethiopia, and after those two compelling circumstances were resolved, because of the gap created by the sports association's board chairman remaining in legal custody; for this he said, "We ask the assembly for forgiveness."

a4864.speaker: Audit report by an independent accountant presented to the general assembly
a4864.speech: Stated that the club's net assets at this time are 13,010,692 birr, and noted that the income the sports association ought to have received from partner organisations, particularly over the past five years, had declined greatly; that there had been delays in paying the salaries of players and employees; that the association currently has debts of 163,832,000 birr owed to service-providing institutions as well as in unpaid salary tax and pension, of which 22 million birr was owed to the club's president, Ato Abnet Gebremeskel; and included 41 million birr presented as uncollected from partner organisations.

a4864.speaker: Five-year plan performance report presented to the general assembly
a4864.speech: Stated that the holding of the Ethiopian Premier League in only certain cities after the COVID-19 pandemic had greatly shaken the club's finances; that the sports association had taken over a 10,000 square metre plot in Lemi Kura Sub-city, of which 2,000 square metres had been taken because of corridor development, leaving it waiting to receive a new title deed; and that the Kibur Ydnekachew Tessema Academy built in Bishoftu town is now serving as the main team's camp and was handed to private organisations to be looked after so that it would not be damaged.

a4864.speaker: Ato Abnet Gebremeskel, longtime chairman of the board of Saint George Sports Association
a4864.speech: Presented a report on the sports association's current issues by means of the internet, before comments were invited on the plan performance and the audit report.

a4864.speaker: Ethiopian Football Federation (observer at the assembly)
a4864.speech: Commenting on the conduct of the assembly, particularly from the standpoint of directives and regulations, raised the question: "Does the sports association's bylaw allow a report to be presented via the internet?"

a4864.speaker: Members of the general assembly (commenters from the floor)
a4864.speech: "The report presented indicates that the venerable Saint George Sports Association is at present in a severe struggle for survival. Responsible for all this problem is the failure to hold the general assembly that legally should have been held every year, and for this, at this assembly, [the board] has completed its term of service. A legal body needs to be designated for this. Holding an election without the situation being investigated by an independent body is neither proper nor legal." ; "How can an audit report called a five-year report be presented when it was not presented, approved and commented upon at a general assembly each year? Does the 41 million birr audit finding presented as uncollected from partner organisations mean that the agreement, when it was first made, was not based on law? And if so, why was it not possible to pursue and enforce the matter legally? The sports association's clubhouse activity was not included in the audit report; why?" ; "While the venerable Saint George Sports Association faces all this danger to its existence, would it not be better to establish a solution-seeking committee that would calmly examine and evaluate the problem and hand over to a properly legal board?" ; "You should not deny us the chance to speak."

a4864.speaker: Chair of the assembly (the podium)
a4864.speech: "Enough comments" ; in response to the call for a solution-seeking committee: "Does our club's bylaw permit this? If the question is amended, gladly."

a4864.speaker: Ato Bahiru Tilahun, Chief Executive of the Ethiopian Football Federation
a4864.speech: Was heard giving repeated reminders as the murmuring and shouting in the hall could not be stopped.

a4864.speaker: Ato Belay Dejene, head of the Addis Ababa City Youth and Sports Bureau
a4864.speech: "I apologise very much for being present at your assembly uncalled and uninvited" ; delivering a strong directive: "I came because the security bureau said that disputes had broken out, in order to calm things down and to advise you to conduct your assembly in peace. We do not want Saint George supporters to be split in two because of an election; although Saint George is a club owned by a popular organisation, it is nevertheless our city's team, which should not be forgotten. Therefore, as a city administration, the matter concerns us."

a4888.speaker: Ahmed Moallim Fiqi, Somali Defense Minister
a4888.speech: says relations with Türkiye are at their highest level, while expressing a desire to implement major projects together ; recalled a pivotal visit to Mogadishu by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and his delegation in 2011 during a time when the al-Shabaab terrorist group had surrounded the Somali capital. “I remember that day. Indeed, just a few days later the city was liberated, and the capital has since enjoyed 14 years of independence and stability.” ; said Mogadishu was not secure during then-Prime Minister Erdogan’s 2011 visit, and remembered the hunger and difficult conditions faced by the Somali people at the time ; “We are truly in a better place today, and I see this relationship progressing day by day,” highlighting that Türkiye’s largest embassy is located in Somalia and expressing confidence that the partnership will endure.

a4888.speaker: Ahmed Moallim Fiqi, Somali Defense Minister (military and economic cooperation)
a4888.speech: pointed to the memorandum of understanding signed between the defense ministries of Somalia and Türkiye, noting the presence of advanced Turkish-made military helicopters flying overhead and armored vehicles in use by Somali forces. “Under the framework of the memorandum of understanding, (Somali) Special Forces have also been trained by Türkiye at the TURKSOM Military Training Base.” ; said they aim to launch major projects and underscored the importance of strengthening economic cooperation, particularly to support the East African country’s stability.

a4982.speaker: United Nations (statement)
a4982.speech: said the conference brought together over 15,000 participants, including nearly 50 heads of state and government, to address the estimated $4 trillion annual SDG financing gap in developing countries ; said the Sevilla Commitment and platform for action outline specific measures aimed at furthering progress towards the SDGs and emphasise the role of international cooperation ; noted that the Sevilla commitment focuses on three main areas: increasing investment for sustainable development, addressing issues related to debt and development and reforming international financial structures, and that the communique includes over 130 initiatives concerning implementation, capacity building, monitoring, and evaluation.

a4982.speaker: Data cited at the conference
a4982.speech: According to data cited, approximately 3 billion people live in countries allocating more funds to interest payments than to health or education.

a4982.speaker: Carlos Cuerpo, Spanish Economy Minister
a4982.speech: stated at the closing press conference that the outcomes aim to support multilateral cooperation and efforts to advance sustainable development globally.

a4982.speaker: Amina Mohammed, United Nations Deputy Secretary-General
a4982.speech: said in her closing remarks: "the human consequences of rising debt burdens, escalating trade tensions and steep cuts to official development assistance have been brought into sharp relief this week. Yet, against this sobering backdrop, the Sevilla conference delivered a strong response a unifying outcome document focused on solutions that reaffirms the Addis Ababa commitments made a decade ago, renews hope through the SDGs, and shows that multilateral cooperation still matters and still works. Let FFD4 be remembered as a conference where the world chose cooperation over fragmentation, unity over division and action over inertia."

a4994.speaker: Radhouane Nouice, United Nations designated expert on Human Rights in Sudan
a4994.speech: Commended Ethiopia's hospitality in housing nearly 300,000 Sudanese refugees, as he briefed on the devastating conditions in the embattled country at the Economic Commission of Africa (ECA) headquarters last week.

a4994.speaker: Radhouane Nouice, United Nations designated expert on Human Rights in Sudan
a4994.speech: Indicated that, with 20 million in need of assistance, 4.5 million displaced from their homes and the destruction of health infrastructure in the country, efforts for humanitarian assistance are hampered by a shortage of funding, inability to obtain visas and blockage of access; he called for the cessation of "the senseless conflict" as he outlined the horrendous living conditions where summary executions, widespread assault and violence were cited as tragic developments: "There are no winners, with only the people losing."

a4997.speaker: Austin Kawah and Kelvin Demey, radio journalists (report 'A Railway Reborn: An exclusive look inside ArcelorMittal Liberia's bold upgrade and expansion of Liberia's railway')
a4997.speech: Produced a report following a sudden investigative tour of ArcelorMittal Liberia's facilities, mainly its railway, of which The Analyst obtained a syndicated copy, as published unedited on page 2 of this edition.

a4997.speaker: Engineers at ArcelorMittal Liberia
a4997.speech: The engineers we spoke with explained that these steel sleepers have a life expectancy of about 50 years—an investment in the future.

a4997.speaker: ArcelorMittal Liberia company officials
a4997.speech: Company officials stressed that this rail line belongs to the people of Liberia, and it's up to all of us—local communities, government, and companies alike—to protect this critical asset.

a5160.speaker: Several American media outlets
a5160.speech: Reported on Wednesday that an official responsible for oversight of the US international aid agency USAID was fired by the government shortly after the publication of a report on the consequences of its dismantling.

a5160.speaker: The Washington Post
a5160.speech: Reported that Paul Martin, inspector general for USAID, received an email on Tuesday from a member of the White House informing him “that on behalf of President Donald Trump (...) your role as inspector general of the United States Agency for International Development is terminated, effective immediately.”

a5160.speaker: Member of the White House (email to Paul Martin)
a5160.speech: “On behalf of President Donald Trump (...) your role as inspector general of the United States Agency for International Development is terminated, effective immediately.”

a5160.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5160.speech: Intends to put an end to the “problems of fraud, waste, abuse” of the many American government bodies, and accuses USAID of misconduct, asserting that “corruption” there is “at levels never seen before,” without substantiating his statement.

a5160.speaker: USAID Office of the Inspector General report published on Monday
a5160.speech: Examines the “risks and challenges for safeguarding and distributing USAID’s $8.2 billion in humanitarian aid funds that are committed but not disbursed” as a result of the suspension of foreign aid programs decided by the State Department and the staff cuts, “which have considerably reduced the operational capacity of its Bureau for Humanitarian Assistance (BHA)” ; estimates that the staff reduction will limit the BHA’s capacity “to prevent humanitarian aid from being diverted because of possible links with terrorist groups, and to monitor aid deliveries in high-risk environments” ; and finds that the aid suspension makes uncertain the situation of “more than $489 million of food aid in ports, in transit and in warehouses,” which risks deteriorating and being diverted.

a5166.speaker: Jerolinmek Piah, Liberian Information Minister
a5166.speech: Said the move by the Government is based on an audit report from the General Auditing Commission (GAC); revealed that the GAC’s report shows that the Management of the Green Park has only been collecting money from Liberians with no accountability and impact in return. “The Management of the Green Park entered a twenty-year verbal agreement with past authorities of the MCC, and that the Management has no records of competence to handle such business.”

a5166.speaker: General Auditing Commission (GAC) audit report
a5166.speech: Shows that the Management of the Green Park has only been collecting money from Liberians with no accountability and impact in return.

a5461.speaker: Proverbs 11:3 (NIV)
a5461.speech: "The integrity of the upright guides them, but the unfaithful are destroyed by their duplicity."

a5521.speaker: Tina Guthrie, Canada’s Ambassador to Burkina Faso
a5521.speech: Hailed the more than 60 years of friendship and cooperation that bind Burkina Faso and Canada; stressed that this cooperation translates into concrete actions in the humanitarian, economic and health fields: “Nearly 17 million school meals have been served, including in areas facing major security challenges, while supporting 9,000 local producers for the supply of school canteens. Our humanitarian aid has reached 1.6 million displaced or vulnerable people. In northern Burkina Faso, Canada is also helping to strengthen access to health care in conflict-affected areas.”

a5521.speaker: Tina Guthrie, Canada’s Ambassador to Burkina Faso
a5521.speech: Noted that Canadian companies present in Burkina Faso create employment, wealth and innovation, while respecting national norms and the highest international standards: “Canadian mining companies continue to play a leading role in the development of Burkina Faso’s mining sector. They have maintained their operations, and one mining plant is even expanding, proof of a long-term commitment to Burkina Faso.”

a5521.speaker: Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré, Burkina Faso’s Minister of Foreign Affairs
a5521.speech: Expressed the Burkinabè government’s gratitude to the Canadian people and hailed Canada’s efforts in the development of the Burkinabè private sector: “Burkina and Canada is more than 60 years of walking together and of cooperation, in which we have learned to know one another, to identify projects together, to carry them out and to undertake new actions in several fields. Today we have enough hindsight to appreciate this cooperation, which has made it possible to obtain concrete results on the ground in various sectors. We try to situate our partners in a spirit of win-win balance. Today, Canada, which has invested a great deal in the mining sector, has enabled Burkina Faso to have a certain coordination, to become aware of its potential and to improve its mining management policy.”

a5576.speaker: Alghabass Ag Intalla, leader of the Azawad Liberation Front (FLA)
a5576.speech: Stressed in his statements that “Africa’s borders are artificial, drawn with a ruler by the colonisers, without respect for our peoples or our lands”, asserting that these boundaries have torn apart families and tribes and cut off nomadic routes that had linked people for centuries ; insists that the Tuareg people, dispersed among Mali, Niger, Algeria, Libya and Burkina Faso, are united by their blood, their culture and their history, and that they are neither a minority nor a tribe, but a single people of the Sahara who must recover their historical unity.

a5576.speaker: New Lines Institute, American think tank (report)
a5576.speech: Recently published a report which proposes an immediate American intervention in southern Algeria, but specifies that this intervention should not be military; the report suggests supporting local research through Algerian institutions, favouring targeted aid mechanisms and mobilising Tuareg diaspora organisations as civic intermediaries.

a5576.speaker: Observers
a5576.speech: Believe that the “Greater Azawad” project could also benefit from implicit support from Europe, and particularly from France, a strategic ally of the United States within NATO; according to them, a Tuareg state aligned with Western interests would offer France considerable political and economic leverage, while weakening Algerian sovereignty.

a5576.speaker: Experts
a5576.speech: Indicate that humanitarian organisations will be mobilised in southern Algeria to document the situation and report alleged human rights violations, while giving international legitimacy to an indirect diplomatic intervention.

a5576.speaker: Experts
a5576.speech: Consider that Algeria must adopt a proactive and comprehensive strategy, that strengthening security in the south through military measures adapted to the terrain and civil initiatives aimed at stabilising local populations is indispensable, and add that the state must also play a mediating role between the FLA and the Malian government, as it did during the 2015 negotiations, in order to prevent any spread of Malian instability onto its territory.

a5608.speaker: Moroccan Ministry of Foreign Affairs (press statement)
a5608.speech: indicates that His Majesty King Mohammed VI, President of the Al-Quds Committee, ordered the immediate delivery to Gaza of nearly 180 tonnes of foodstuffs, children’s milk, medicines, surgical equipment and emergency shelters; this vital cargo, which also includes tents and blankets, will be transported through a specially arranged corridor to guarantee its direct delivery to the Palestinian population.

a5608.speaker: Humanitarian agencies
a5608.speech: are warning of cases of infant deaths for lack of baby milk, and of the collapse of health services.

a5769.speaker: Medicines Control Agency (MCA) of The Gambia
a5769.speech: Issued an urgent warning to the public, declaring it illegal to import, distribute, store, or sell medical devices, including in vitro diagnostics, without proper authorization in The Gambia; the announcement, made under the Medicines and Related Products Act of 2014, underscores the agency’s mandate to ensure the quality, safety, and efficacy of medicines and related products ; said all individuals and entities engaged in the trade of medical devices are required to obtain authorization from the MCA and that noncompliance with the Medicines and Related Substances Act, 1965, and the Medicines and Related Substances Regulations, 2011, will result in severe regulatory sanctions

a5769.speaker: Medicines Control Agency (MCA) of The Gambia
a5769.speech: Highlighted global concerns over substandard and falsified medical devices, particularly in vitro diagnostics, which can produce inaccurate laboratory results, leading to misdiagnoses, improper treatment, and increased health risks, such as higher morbidity and mortality; citing recommendations from the World Health Organization and the African Union, the agency emphasized the need for stringent regulation to protect public safety

a5769.speaker: World Health Organization and African Union (recommendations)
a5769.speech: Cited by the MCA as recommending stringent regulation of medical devices to protect public safety

a5779.speaker: Abdoulaye Diop, Malian Minister of Foreign Affairs
a5779.speech: Said in an exclusive interview with RIA Novosti that he is in Moscow with his colleagues, the foreign ministers of Burkina Faso and Niger, at the invitation of Sergei Lavrov, in the framework of consultations between the Confederation of the Alliance of Sahel States and Russia; said the consultations demonstrated that Russia and the Sahel countries share a common vision of their international obligations, based on respect for sovereignty and sovereign choice, on fighting together against imperialism, neocolonialism, the subordination of their countries, the instrumentalisation of human rights and interference in internal affairs.

a5779.speaker: Abdoulaye Diop, Malian Minister of Foreign Affairs
a5779.speech: Said they wanted to build a strategic partnership between Russia and the Sahel countries, first of all on peace and security, wanting Russia to accompany the Confederation mechanism by supporting the joint military operations they conduct on the ground, with the prospect of creating a joint force; said they also wanted to strengthen diplomatic cooperation so their countries speak with one voice internationally, noting that “Russia needs our countries, we need Russia as a permanent member of the UN Security Council”; said the third aspect concerns development — economic integration, infrastructure, railways, roads, energy, agricultural projects, mineral resources and the creation of an investment bank; said they had very frank and open discussions, noted Russia’s firm will to continue working with them, and agreed to institutionalise the consultation mechanism, meeting at least once a year alternately in Russia and in the Sahel region, with a monitoring mechanism, which he considers an important step marking the progressive recognition of the new geopolitical reality that the AES represents.

a5779.speaker: Abdoulaye Diop, Malian Minister of Foreign Affairs
a5779.speech: Said on a possible Sahel-Russia summit that it is not excluded a priori and was not openly discussed, but the mechanism exists and depends on the will of the heads of state; said President Vladimir Putin, like the heads of state of Burkina Faso (Captain Ibrahim Traoré), Niger (General Abdourahamane Tiani) and Mali (Army General Assimi Goïta), have much in common and a truly common vision of their problems, consult each other regularly, and that he does not exclude that one day they decide to meet in this or a more appropriate format; said the ministers, with their colleague Sergei Lavrov, will continue this political activity and these consultations, as will their ambassadors.

a5779.speaker: Abdoulaye Diop, Malian Minister of Foreign Affairs
a5779.speech: Said on armaments autonomy that they are already working with Russia on several projects, that their countries want to strengthen their capacities and develop their autonomy to escape models of dependence, that the acquisition of military equipment will be a growing need and their countries will not continue simply to import it; said it is important that their partner Russia not oppose technology transfer and the strengthening of their production capacities; said President Goïta has the ambition to develop the military industry in Mali and there is a desire to create production capacities at the Sahel level, which would reduce dependence on imports while creating jobs.

a5779.speaker: Abdoulaye Diop, Malian Minister of Foreign Affairs
a5779.speech: Said on visas and travel documents that these questions are linked to the desire to ensure the free movement of citizens and to facilitate the movement of guests, tourists and partners; said the visa question is an initiative of the heads of state, experts have analysed it and made proposals, and it is now on the agenda of the ministers — a project under way; said the AES passport and biometric identity card were adopted in January by Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger, meet technical standards going beyond the usual ICAO requirements, and that official notification procedures were followed with ICAO and all interested states, first for the ordinary passport and then for diplomatic and service passports.

a5779.speaker: Abdoulaye Diop, Malian Minister of Foreign Affairs
a5779.speech: Said on languages that it is a goal they welcome if Russian experts or Russia as a state decide to work with their countries to promote their languages; said the development of national languages is a political objective and absolute priority, while they are not closed to using working languages — Russian, French or English; said cultural relations with Russia do not date from today but go back to the first years of independence, with thousands of Malians who speak Russian and were trained in the former USSR and now in Russia; said they support all efforts to master other languages and welcome and encourage these initiatives as contributing to mutual understanding and to strengthening commercial and cultural ties.

a5779.speaker: Abdoulaye Diop, Malian Minister of Foreign Affairs
a5779.speech: Said on the halt of the USAID programme: “Personally, I am not shocked by this decision. Moreover, the Malian government was not shocked either.” He said the first lesson is that for several months Mali had been negotiating with USAID and the negotiations were extremely difficult and reached a deadlock, because the way American aid was distributed in Mali did not allow Malians to determine their own priorities or to choose the NGOs implementing projects, and the funds allocated did not even pass through the state budget — which is why Mali objected on the principle of national sovereignty in development; if a foreign partner wants to implement programmes in Mali, it must be done with the participation of the state or in agreement with the Malian government. He said the second lesson is that when these countries decide overnight to suspend their aid, it means the aid was not provided to their peoples but was an instrument or lever of foreign policy to achieve certain objectives. The third lesson is that their countries must be realistic and cannot build their plans on the interests of others; these sources of aid will dry up or diminish sooner or later, because there are countries that refuse aid completely if they do not vote for them on an issue or if political changes occur. He said they must therefore find mechanisms to finance their countries through national resources and identify international resources free from these political diktats, noting that mechanisms exist within the BRICS or other associations, and that African countries must draw lessons.

a5779.speaker: Abdoulaye Diop, Malian Minister of Foreign Affairs
a5779.speech: Said on the partial Russia-Ukraine ceasefire that peace between Russia and Ukraine would benefit the whole world, both for stability and for the world economy and their own economies, which is why they support it and encourage Russia to continue its efforts to reach peace with its neighbour; said Mali expresses its solidarity with Russia, as the AES supports Russia in this struggle. However, he noted that for Mali, which has broken off relations with Ukraine, “Ukraine is a terrorist state”: Ukraine has openly expressed its support for terrorist groups in the Sahel, particularly in Mali, which led to the deaths of many soldiers and citizens; “We condemn these acts and believe that Ukraine must be held responsible. African peoples must consider it a source of instability in our region, an irresponsible actor that threatens our security.” He added that this does not prevent them from wishing for peace between Russia and Ukraine, and that if that peace allows Ukrainian and Russian products, including grain and fertiliser, to be freely supplied to countries that need them, that is good; Mali and the AES as a whole support all initiatives leading to peace — but a just and lasting peace that takes account of Russia’s legitimate security considerations.

a5779.speaker: Diana Al-Hashem, RIA Novosti journalist (interviewer)
a5779.speech: Asked, among other questions, what was discussed with the Russian side and what was agreed; whether a Sahel-Russia summit is planned; whether Moscow offers help with the Sahel countries’ military-industrial autonomy; when the common visa policy can be implemented and whether the single AES passport is accepted in Russia; whether Russia could help Mali preserve and develop local languages; whether the halt of the USAID programme affected Mali and what measures were taken to minimise the consequences; and how he assesses the partial Russia-Ukraine ceasefire and the importance of resuming Russian grain and fertiliser exports for Mali and the Sahel.

a6123.speaker: Green Climate Fund (GCF)
a6123.speech: Said it will make its largest ever series of investments and speed up dealmaking as it looks to help poorer nations respond to global warming.

a6123.speaker: OECD (June report)
a6123.speech: Said official development assistance could fall 17% this year after a 9% drop in 2024, led by hefty cuts to U.S. aid by President Donald Trump.

a6123.speaker: Seyni Nafo, GCF Co-Chair
a6123.speech: “At a time when collective climate action is more needed than ever, GCF is stepping up to deliver on its mandate,” said in a statement.

a6347.speaker: Peoples Democratic Party (PDP)
a6347.speech: Announced last week that it would zone the presidency to the South in 2027.

a6347.speaker: Festus Keyamo (SAN), Aviation Minister, and Chidi Odinkalu, rights activist
a6347.speech: Are among the most recent to flag the legal risk that the courts might overturn former President Goodluck Jonathan's candidature because of a constitutional amendment (after he left office in 2015), which bars him – or anyone twice sworn in – from retaking the oath of office.

a6347.speaker: The PDP and a relative of the former president, suspected of speaking for him
a6347.speech: Have told the Aviation Minister, Festus Keyamo (SAN), and rights activist, Chidi Odinkalu, to mind their business.

a6347.speaker: Goodluck Jonathan, former President of Nigeria
a6347.speech: Out of frustration, he once said that he believed elements in his government were working for the insurgents.

a6347.speaker: NEITI report
a6347.speech: A NEITI report said Nigeria lost about 268 million barrels of crude oil between 2009 and 2015 due to oil theft and pipeline vandalism. The cost in 2013 alone was $8 billion.

a6616.speaker: Le Monde Afrique
