a6616.speech: Sees the removal of Tidjane Thiam from the electoral rolls as a "thunderclap," stressing that Thiam was considered the main opponent of President Alassane Ouattara, who, at 83, could seek a fourth term in October 2025.

a6616.speaker: Tidjane Thiam, opposition figure and designated candidate of the PDCI-RDA (on Abidjan.net)
a6616.speech: Denounces an "unjust, unjustified and incomprehensible" exclusion, accusing those in power of having used a judicial veneer to eliminate their political rival.

a6616.speaker: Emile Ebrotie, spokesperson of the Independent Electoral Commission (CEI)
a6616.speech: Attempts nonetheless to give reassurance about the transparency of the electoral process.

a6616.speaker: Sud Quotidien (Senegalese newspaper)
a6616.speech: Highlights the repercussions of this removal after Thiam renounced his French nationality, speaking of "a thin line between Ivoirite and Statelessness."

a6616.speaker: L'AS (Senegalese newspaper)
a6616.speech: Warns of the risks of instability, referring to a president "who is playing with matches," a reference to the post-electoral crisis of 2010.

a6616.speaker: Le Monde Afrique
a6616.speech: Expresses concern about the withdrawal of USAID, the American development aid agency, from Liberia; this disengagement leaves the country "on the edge of the abyss," given that this aid constituted an essential share of the national budget.

a6616.speaker: Le Nouveau Reveil (Malian newspaper)
a6616.speech: Criticises the emergence of "a new oligarchy without scruples," denouncing the betrayal of the promises made when multipartyism was introduced in 1991.

a6616.speaker: L'Alternance (Malian newspaper)
a6616.speech: Observes a collective awakening of the political parties, which are setting aside their divisions to form a united front against a plan to dissolve them deemed unconstitutional - an unprecedented sacred union aimed at defending their own political survival and, more broadly, the democratic foundations of the country. The paper asks: "How far will they go in their fight for the Republic?"

a6616.speaker: Jeune Afrique
a6616.speech: Raises a shocking hypothesis: "what if Bassirou Diomaye Faye refused to pay the country's debts?", in the wake of the ongoing audit of public finances - a strategy the magazine judges to be "high risk."

a6616.speaker: L'Observateur (Senegalese newspaper)
a6616.speech: Reveals that the National Assembly is preparing to examine the indictment files of two former ministers, Mansour Faye and Moustapha Diop, for alleged embezzlement of public funds.

a6762.speaker: Nobel Committee
a6762.speech: Said the two economists were honoured "for their theory of interactive decision-making, which can be applied to security and disarmament policy, to market price formation, and to political and economic negotiations" ; said their ideas "proved to be of great relevance for the resolution of conflicts and efforts to avoid wars."

a6762.speaker: Thomas Schelling, economist and Nobel laureate
a6762.speech: Argued that, in a nuclear war, the capacity to retaliate against an attack is more important than the capacity to withstand an attack, and that the uncertainty as to whether retaliation will in fact occur matters more than the guarantee of a counter-attack ; concluded that the mere threat can be used as a weapon to deter the adversary, and that to convince the adversary of one's willingness to press the "nuclear button" it is enough to seem mad enough to do it.

a6762.speaker: Jim Sciutto, CNN journalist
a6762.speech: Published in October 2020 a book titled "The Madman Theory: Trump Takes On the World", in which he gives examples of episodes in which Trump was unpredictable during his first term, notably in relation to North Korean leader Kim Jong-un.

a6762.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
a6762.speech: Nicknamed Kim Jong-un "rocket man" and stated that he would respond with "fire and fury", projecting an image of unpredictability.

a6762.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
a6762.speech: Recently proposed that the USA "take control" of the Gaza Strip and remove some two million people, resettling them permanently in neighbouring countries, after which the territory would be rebuilt and transformed into the new "Riviera of the Middle East."

a6835.speaker: Nkaku Kabi, All Basotho Convention (ABC) leader
a6835.speech: Has expressed grave concern over the escalating youth unemployment crisis in Lesotho and attacked the government for “doing very little” to address the problem ; claimed that while past ABC led coalitions had been better at tackling youth unemployment, Prime Minister Sam Matekane’s Revolution for Prosperity (RFP) led administration was absolutely clueless ; said not only had the RFP failed to fulfil its grandiose promises to all Basotho, it had particularly failed the youths who had catapulted it to power ; “Despite the many promises made during the 2022 elections, the youth of Lesotho remain in peril, facing a future filled with uncertainty and hopelessness.” ; “The foundation of our politics is rooted in slavery and exploitation, and yet we have not learned from our past. Our mineral wealth has not translated into prosperity for our people, especially the youth who are our future.” ; pointed to a recent recruitment event for the Lesotho Defence Force (LDF) where over 10,000 youths showed up in Maseru while thousands more did the same across Lesotho’s ten districts, hoping to secure one of just 500 available positions as soldiers: “This turnout underscores the severity of the crisis we are facing. It’s a stark reminder that African politics can be unforgiving, and we owe it to our young people to create better opportunities.”

a6835.speaker: Nkaku Kabi, All Basotho Convention (ABC) leader
a6835.speech: Claimed that youth unemployment had been better during the period of coalitions led by his ABC between 2012-2015 and 2017-2020; said the ABC had launched “successful initiatives” such as block farming, which he claimed had not only alleviated poverty but also created “numerous” jobs; reminisced about ex-Premier Thabane’s government’s success in convincing textile industry owners to increase wages from M1,500 for the lowest paid to more than M2000 ; “When we were in power, we raised factory workers’ wages and prioritized agriculture. We need to remember that agriculture can provide lasting solutions to our employment crisis.” ; claimed mockingly that while the RFP had failed to deliver on its promises, “the ABC has a proven track record of effective governance”.

a6835.speaker: Nkaku Kabi, All Basotho Convention (ABC) leader
a6835.speech: Said the future of Lesotho’s textile industry, which employs 31,000 workers, now looks bleak after the US government’s decision to nullify the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA).

a6835.speaker: Nkaku Kabi, All Basotho Convention (ABC) leader
a6835.speech: Attacked Mr Matekane and his allies of concentrating on lining their pockets instead of fulfilling their promised mandate: “We see our leaders being more focused on personal gain rather than on the welfare of the people. The promises made to the youth during the electoral campaign have not been realized, and we cannot sit idly by while our young people suffer.” ; “It is time for Mr Matekane and his government to open their ears and their hearts to the plight of our youth.”

a6835.speaker: Nkaku Kabi, All Basotho Convention (ABC) leader
a6835.speech: Called for collaborative efforts across all sectors of society to tackle youth unemployment, suggesting that land resources should be redirected for agricultural use rather than housing; said that across Lesotho, Basotho who rely on agriculture were increasingly selling their land to property developers, gradually diminishing the country’s limited arable land, which makes up only 11 percent of Lesotho’s total land area; said the primary driver behind this shift is widespread poverty among Basotho who, faced with economic hardship, were opting to sell their agricultural land rather than sustaining their traditional farming activities ; “We need to be forward-thinking. Our land is underutilized, and it has the potential to solve the unemployment crisis if we approach it with the right mindset.” ; proposed the establishment of a forum where experts can discuss innovative solutions for youth employment and urged the government to allocate M20 million from each ministry towards youth job creation initiatives, insisting that meaningful dialogue is necessary for progress.

a6835.speaker: Dr Retṣelisitsoe Matlanyane, Minister of Finance and Development Planning of Lesotho (2025-2026 annual budget speech to Parliament, 19 February)
a6835.speech: Said 38 percent of Basotho youth were unemployed with females bearing the biggest brunt.

a7117.speaker: US District Judge Paul A. Engelmayer (court order)
a7117.speech: Issued a preliminary injunction on Saturday to prohibit access, ordering Musk and his team to immediately destroy any copies of records; the order said the states would "face irreparable" harm without immediate relief: "That is both because of the risk that the new policy presents of the disclosure of sensitive and confidential information and the heightened risk that the systems in question will be more vulnerable than before to hacking," the order read. The order restrains the defendants from granting access to Treasury Department records containing personally identifiable or confidential information to special government employees, political appointees, and other employees from outside the department.

a7117.speaker: 19 state attorneys general (lawsuit)
a7117.speech: They argued access for Musk, a "special government employee", and Doge, which is not an official government department, violated federal law.

a7117.speaker: White House, President Donald Trump and Elon Musk (non-response)
a7117.speech: There was no immediate comment from the White House, President Donald Trump or Musk.

a7121.speaker: Sources (anonymous, spoke to the Daily Graphic)
a7121.speech: Sources have told the Daily Graphic that all the arrests are in connection with the same investigation ; the OSP, sources confirmed, is examining the procurement processes, the scope of services rendered, and the justification for the payments made under the contracts, and is also seeking to verify SML's claims that its operations have led to significant revenue savings for the country.

a7121.speaker: Strategic Mobilisation Limited (SML)
a7121.speech: Claims that its operations have led to significant revenue savings for the country.

a7121.speaker: Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) (statement)
a7121.speech: The statement by the OSP indicated that the investigations into the SML issues were remarkable in the nation's anti-corruption efforts "and suggests a renewed resolve by the OSP to confront high-level corruption in public financial management".

a7121.speaker: Civil society organisations and anti-corruption campaigners
a7121.speech: Had called for full transparency and accountability in the matter.

a7121.speaker: Sources (anonymous)
a7121.speech: Said the separate arrests by the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO), of the former CEO of the Buffer Stock Company, Abdul Hannan, and one other person, were effected in Accra and Tamale in a coordinated move by the anti-graft institution.

a7207.speaker: Fardowsa Isman Egal, Minister of Transport and Civil Aviation of Somalia
a7207.speech: Said that the allocation was made to support the historical bilateral relation between Somalia and China, and to acknowledge China's contribution to the development and humanitarian assistance of Somalia; urged the organizations occupying the land to relocate quickly and make way for the construction of the new Chinese embassy; said that the new embassy will improve the Chinese embassy's services to the public, such as visa processing and trade facilitation.

a7207.speaker: Chen Wendi, Charge d'Affaires of the Chinese Embassy in Somalia
a7207.speech: Expressed his gratitude and acceptance of the allocation; said that the new land will help the embassy to expand its functions and to better serve the interests of both countries; thanked minister Fardowsa and the officials from the ministry of foreign affairs, the civil aviation and the airport authority of Somalia for their cooperation and support; said that the allocation will strengthen the cooperation and brotherly relation between Somalia and China, and that China will continue to stand by Somalia in its pursuit of peace and prosperity.

a7350.speaker: A senior US official (anonymous)
a7350.speech: said on Wednesday that nearly 500 tonnes of high-energy biscuits, to be used as emergency food for malnourished young children, expired this month while sitting in a warehouse in Dubai.

a7350.speaker: Michael Rigas, US Deputy Secretary of State in charge of management
a7350.speech: Under questioning by lawmakers, tied the decision to the dismantling of the US Agency for International Development (USAID), which closed its doors on July 1: “I think that this was just a casualty of the shutdown of USAID,” adding that he was “distressed” that the food went to waste.

a7350.speaker: Michael Rigas, US Deputy Secretary of State in charge of management
a7350.speech: said that the US remained the world’s largest donor, and he promised to learn further details about the biscuits: “I do want to find out what happened here and get to the ground truth.”

a7350.speaker: Two internal USAID memos reviewed by Reuters (dated May 5 and May 19) and four sources familiar with the matter
a7350.speech: Aid officials managed to save 622 tonnes of the energy-dense biscuits in June – sending them to Syria, Bangladesh and Myanmar – but 496 tonnes, worth $793,000 before they expired this month, will be destroyed.

a7350.speaker: Two sources (anonymous)
a7350.speech: said the wasted biscuits will be sent to landfills or incinerated in the United Arab Emirates.

a7350.speaker: Internal USAID memo of May 5 (verified by three sources familiar with the matter)
a7350.speech: That will cost the US government an additional $100,000, according to the May 5 memo.

a7350.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a7350.speech: has said the US pays disproportionately for foreign aid, and he wants other countries to shoulder more of the burden.

a7350.speaker: The Trump administration
a7350.speech: announced plans to shut down USAID in January, leaving more than 60,000 tonnes of food aid stuck in stores around the world.

a7350.speaker: Reuters
a7350.speech: reported in May that more than 60,000 tonnes of food aid was stuck in stores around the world.

a7350.speaker: United Nations World Food Programme (WFP)
a7350.speech: The food aid stuck in Dubai was fortified wheat biscuits, which are calorie-rich and typically deployed in crisis conditions where people lack cooking facilities, “providing immediate nutrition for a child or adult”, according to the WFP.

a7350.speaker: Senator Tim Kaine, a Democrat
a7350.speech: said lawmakers had specifically raised the issue of the food with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio in March ; “A government that is put on notice – here are resources that will save 27,000 starving kids, can you please distribute them or give them to someone who can? Who decides, no, we would rather keep the warehouse locked, let the food expire, and then burn it?”

a7350.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a7350.speech: In May, he promised lawmakers that no food aid would be wasted.

a7350.speaker: US government data
a7350.speech: The US disbursed $61bn in foreign assistance last year, just over half of it via USAID, according to government data.

a7350.speaker: United Nations (recorded contributions)
a7350.speech: The US is the world’s largest humanitarian aid donor, amounting to at least 38 percent of all contributions recorded by the UN.

a7350.speaker: The Trump administration
a7350.speech: notified Congress in March that USAID would fire almost all of its staff in two rounds on July 1 and September 2, as it prepared to shut down.

a7350.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State (statement of July 1)
a7350.speech: In a statement on July 1 marking the transfer of USAID to the State Department, Rubio said the US was abandoning what he called a charity-based model and would focus on empowering countries to grow sustainably.

a7350.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
a7350.speech: says 319 million people have limited access to food worldwide; of those, 1.9 million people are gripped by catastrophic hunger and on the brink of famine, primarily in Gaza and Sudan.

a7379.speaker: The New York Times (report)
a7379.speech: Reported that United States President Donald Trump's administration is mulling a new travel ban that is expected to affect citizens from dozens of countries to varying degrees; quoting anonymous officials, the report published on Friday said the US government's draft list featured 43 countries, divided into three categories of travel restrictions, with a first group of 10 countries set for full visa suspension, a second group of five countries facing partial suspensions, and a third group of 26 countries considered for partial suspension of US visa issuance.

a7379.speaker: US government draft memo
a7379.speech: Said a total of 26 countries including Belarus, Pakistan and Turkmenistan would be considered for a partial suspension of US visa issuance if their governments "do not make efforts to address deficiencies within 60 days."

a7379.speaker: US official (anonymous)
a7379.speech: Told the Reuters news agency there could be changes to the list and it was yet to be approved by the administration, including US Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

a7379.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (executive order of January 20)
a7379.speech: Issued an executive order on January 20 requiring intensified security vetting of any foreigners seeking admission to the US to detect national security threats; the order directed several cabinet members to submit by March 21 a list of countries from which travel should be partly or fully suspended because their "vetting and screening information is so deficient."

a7379.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a7379.speech: Previewed his plan in an October 2023 speech, pledging to restrict people from the Gaza Strip, Libya, Somalia, Syria, Yemen and "anywhere else that threatens our security."

a7443.speaker: United Kingdom government
a7443.speech: Announced Friday that it will host the 17th replenishment pledging session of the African Development Fund (ADF) in December.

a7443.speaker: Baroness Jenny Chapman, UK Minister of State for Development and Africa
a7443.speech: Said the UK intends to make a strong pledge and encouraged all development partners to consider ambitious contributions to the 17th replenishment of the Fund. "The replenishment is an opportunity to signal our collective commitment to Africa's growth and development, its institutions, and to innovative, modern approaches to development finance in a challenging global environment." She noted that the UK remains a key contributor to the Fund, providing substantial financial commitments and strategic engagement that help sustain development impact, even amid a tighter aid budget; also welcomed Dr. Ould Tah's proposal for the UK to host a Private Sector Day for private companies and development finance institutions to explore approaches to foster investment opportunities across Africa.

a7443.speaker: Dr Sidi Ould Tah, African Development Bank Group President
a7443.speech: "The African Development Bank Group welcomes United Kingdom's announcement to host the African Development Fund's 17th replenishment pledging session." He added: "It is a rallying call for a strong ADF-17 replenishment, which is both an investment in Africa's development as well as in shared global prosperity."

a7443.speaker: Centre for Global Development (2021)
a7443.speech: In 2021, recognised the quality of the Fund's development assistance, ranking it second among 49 bilateral and multilateral development agencies.
